production_route.release_rule: Accepted for H2 schematic use because exact identity, Standard-PCBA eligibility, public live stock, MOQ and price were timestamped together. Recheck at architecture freeze and immediately before the exact-one order.

service_vbus.hardware_requirement: An always-on hardware detector and asynchronous latch must seize service ownership without C5 or Hub firmware.

detector.topology: C5 service VBUS -> 1-Mohm top resistor -> MOSFET gate; 1-Mohm gate-to-ground resistor; source to ground; drain is SERVICE_VBUS_PRESENT_N with an AON 10-kohm pull-up
detector.proof: The only service-VBUS DC path is the 2-Mohm divider to ground and the insulated MOSFET gate. No semiconductor junction or product rail is connected to service VBUS. Valid USB VBUS gives at least 2.351 V at the gate, above the exact device's 1.8-V RDS(on) test point; presence therefore pulls the active-low detector node hard low before any application domain is released.

used_gate.function: four-input NAND; CLR_N can go low only when VBUS is absent and all three release proofs are high

release_qualifier.unused_gate: tie all four inputs to SAFETY_GROUND; leave the deterministic-high output unconnected

invariants: PRE_N and CLR_N cannot both be low because SERVICE_VBUS_PRESENT_N is both PRE_N and one input of the clear NAND.
C5, Hub and mux remain in the global AON-POR safe shell until either asynchronous preset or qualified clear has established a valid ownership state.
No C5, Hub or S3 firmware output reaches PRE_N, CLR_N or the VBUS detector.
The explicit AON release request is necessary but cannot clear ownership unless VBUS absence, C5 EN low and Hub SDIO high-Z are simultaneously proven in hardware.
detector_latch_implementation.release_rule: Accepted for native R2 schematic use. Recheck every exact JLC number, Standard-PCBA eligibility, stock/explicit route, MOQ and price at architecture freeze and immediately before the exact-one order.

interboard.connector: FX8C-80P-SV1(92) / FX8C-80S-SV5(92), straight SMT, 80 contacts, 11-mm working gap
interboard.why_not_20_or_60: The current 4.25-A step envelope receives fourteen parallel 3V3_MAIN contacts and fourteen primary return contacts, leaving 0.304 A per power contact versus the 0.4-A rating before H3/H5 thermal proof. After two AON contacts, signal-reference returns and 31 live signals, a 60-contact pair has no controlled reserve; 80 is the smallest current FX8C size that preserves both derating and nine true NC contacts.

locality_contract.rule: Every payload endpoint stays on the board that owns its controller. M1 carries no display bus, nRF/SPI payload, microSD payload, main RF trace or audio stream.

intentional_crossings.hub_rf_ipc: five point-to-point Hub-RF control/data wires are the sole compute-domain message path
intentional_crossings.s3_usb: the rear/bottom power-and-service receptacle reaches the front S3 native USB pair directly
intentional_crossings.encoder: the externally reachable rear encoder remains direct to S3 PCNT plus one local-expander push input
intentional_crossings.safety_and_evidence: AON safety, thermal and TX-evidence nets cross to the rear safety controller by design

interboard.mechanical_load_path: M1 is electrical/alignment only. Four 11.00-mm compression stops, two anti-shear enclosure datums and independent front/rear PCB capture lips constrain the boards when one screw is loose; no drop, installation or enclosure-bending load is accepted through the SMT joints.
interboard.result: R2 uses 31 live signals, fourteen 3V3_MAIN contacts, twenty-four defined returns, two AON contacts and nine true NC reserve contacts; M1-35 carries the latched FAULT_KILL state to the independent front indicator, M1-36 carries the bounded S3 fault-UI reset crossing, five former reserves carry only low-speed AON service/alert state, and no obsolete audio, video or M5 signal remains assigned.

display.panel: EastRising ER-TFT035IPS-6 configured with ER-TPC035-6 capacitive touch; ILI9488 + FT6236
display.interface: dedicated direct i8080-8 (Intel 8080) on S3 LCD_CAM TX with GDMA; D0..D7, WR and DC are direct, CS is hard-low because the bus is exclusive, RD is hard-high, IM[2:0]=011, reset remains on the local slow-I/O output, and front Hub captures TE plus drives reset-off backlight PWM
display.controller_limit_basis: ILI9488 v1.00 section 17.4.1 specifies a 40-ns minimum DBI Type-B write cycle, 15-ns minimum WR high/low widths, and 10-ns data setup/hold. The locked ESP-IDF v6.0.2 i80 driver derives the S3 bus clock from 80 MHz with an integer prescaler: a requested 24 MHz becomes 26.667 MHz and is illegal, while 20 MHz is exact.
display.s3_supported_sources: ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM supports an 8-bit i8080 output and GDMA. With ESP-IDF v6.0.2's standard integer divider, the selected exact 20-MHz write clock gives a 50-ns cycle and nominal 25-ns high/low phases: 10 ns of cycle margin and 10 ns of pulse-width margin against the exact ILI9488 limits.
display.gpio_closure: Twenty-seven of 33 exposed S3 GPIO are assigned: 10 direct i8080 outputs, 5 chip-select-free S3-Hub quad data/clock, 2 UI I2C, 2 USB, 2 encoder, 1 wired-OR UI/Hub alert, BOOT, display reset, touch reset and 2 service-UART lines. Six GPIO remain uncommitted reserves. TE and backlight PWM consume Hub GPIO45/46 instead of S3 pins.
display.fallback: The exact 50-contact panel also exposes ILI9488 4-wire serial mode. A deliberate adapter strap revision can select it only as first-prototype recovery if the i8080 timing gate fails; it is ordinary serial SPI, not QSPI, and is not the preferred interface.
display.maximality_result: Direct i8080-8 at the exact panel-safe 20 MHz matches the former 40-MHz four-lane QSPI raw wire rate while using the panel's fully documented native path, without adding a processor, moving buttons off S3 or sharing display traffic with storage/radio IPC.
display.hil: Before fabrication, compile and run the LCD_TX DMA harness on the emulator-supported register model. H5 then proves ILI9488 IM straps, exact 20-MHz edges, TE timestamp latency and full-frame/dirty-region timing; 25 MHz is the controller limit, a 24-MHz ESP-IDF request is forbidden because it resolves to 26.667 MHz, and neither value is assumed as a production clock.
